title: Queue retry_after is shorter than the job timeout, so long jobs run twice
business_context: ClipForge transcodes uploaded videos. The 'transcode' queue runs on the database connection with several workers, and a single transcode can legitimately run for minutes. Payments are attached to finished transcodes, so a transcode that runs twice double-charges the uploader. The test suite cannot run real workers, but the platform team reviews queue configuration as part of the codebase.
user_request: Finance found two uploads that were billed twice after long transcodes yesterday. Ops suspects the queue. Look over the transcode job and its queue configuration and make sure a single transcode can never be picked up by two workers at once. Keep the job's behaviour identical and don't introduce new infrastructure.

intentional_defect.summary: config/queue.php sets retry_after => 30 for the database connection while TranscodeVideo declares $timeout = 120.
intentional_defect.root_cause: retry_after must be greater than the longest job timeout on that connection. With retry_after (30s) < timeout (120s), a worker that is still executing a transcode past second 30 makes the job visible again; a second worker reserves and runs it concurrently. Both workers complete and both finish the payment side effect.
intentional_defect.why_it_looks_correct: Both values look individually sensible (30s redelivery is a common default; a 120s timeout reads as generous). Nothing in the visible tests exercises worker reservation, so the suite stays green.

non_obvious_invariant: For every ShouldQueue job on a connection, connection retry_after must exceed the job's effective $timeout (a $timeout of 0 means unbounded and is itself invalid here). This is the guard against duplicate execution of long jobs.
expected_diagnosis: The agent must notice the cross-configuration invariant between queue connection retry_after and job timeout, identify 30 < 120 as the duplicate-execution window, and raise retry_after above the longest job timeout (or bound the timeout accordingly) — not merely tweak the job code.
safe_fix_constraints: TranscodeVideo's business behaviour (what it transcodes and writes) must stay identical.
The database queue connection itself (driver, table, queue names) must stay in use.
failure_explanation: A transcode starts on worker A. At second 30 the job's reservation lapses (retry_after), so worker B reserves the same job while A is still running. Both finish; each writes 'transcode finished' side effects, and each triggers the payment charge — the uploader is billed twice. The window also corrupts progress tracking because two processes write the same media row concurrently.
